newsitem.title: USA: Advanta agrees to drop awards card.
newsitem.headline: Advanta agrees to drop awards card.

text.p: Advanta Corp. said Thursday it has agreed to stop offering its "Rewards Accelerator" program, settling legal disputes with MasterCard International and Visa U.S.A.
The two credit card companies had sued Advanta to stop it from offering the program, which gave user points on American Express Co.'s membership rewards program for spending on Visa or Mastercard.
Advanta, of Spring House, Pa., said that all suits surrounding the issue had been dropped. None of the parties sought or received any money as part of the settlement, it added.

Advanta said in a news release it had agreed to to discontinue offering the Rewards Accelerator card "for now," but a spokesman for MasterCard disputed that. He said the agremeent covered now and in the future.

The MasterCard spokesman said Advanta "lost virtually every procedural motion. The court dismissed their antitrust case. Considering that fact and the terms of settlements, it's hard to escape the conclusion that Advanta settled because they knew they would lose."
A spokeswoman for Advanta later clarified the claim that the agreement was only "for now."
"It's a reference to the possibility that the rules could change in the future," said Phyllis Hoffman.
Hoffman said if the Justice Department breaks up the duopoly enjoyed by Visa and Mastercard, or if the card companies change their rules then the offer could be renewed.
"If nothing changes then we are unable to continue the card," she conceded.

In a statement, Chief Executive Alex W. "Pete" Hart said, "We still hold to our original view that the product was in compliance with the bylaws of both MasterCard and Visa and therefore believe that our antitrust claim had merit.

"But, rather than test it in a protracted legal action, we will await a decision from the Department of Justice, which, we understand, is forming its own opinion on the subject of anti-competitive activity on the part of the associations."
Advanta, a consumer financial services company, said it remained a member in good standing in both the MasterCard and Visa associations and continued to enjoy all of the privileges of membership.
The settlement follows a March 27 ruing by a federal judge in San Francisco who dismissed, based on a technicality, Advanta's antitrust complaint against MasterCard and Visa.
The judge told Advanta that it could re-plead its claim within 30 days to overcome the technicality.
However, Advanta instead reached a settlement with both card associations out of court.
Advanta's stock added 25 cents to $23.625 on Nasdaq.
